1: # Native Linux installation
     2: 
     3: ## Current availability
     4: 
     5: The supported deployment shape is a native Linux GNU binary managed by the
     6: systemd system manager. The release qualification targets are x86_64 and
     7: aarch64 with glibc 2.17 or newer. The host needs systemd, kernel WireGuard,
     8: `nftables`, and the Linux capabilities required to manage network interfaces.
     9: The release installer itself is a small Rust binary; Rust, Cargo, Python,
    10: Node, and Docker are not runtime requirements.
    11: 
    12: Releases are checksums-only by maintainer decision: GitHub TLS delivery
    13: plus published SHA-256 digests, with no detached signatures and no
    14: production trust key. `update check` and `update run` fail closed
    15: permanently; every release requires a fresh install. Do not treat a
    16: fixture-signed artifact or a local candidate as a release.
    17: 
    18: ## Install a local candidate
    19: 
    20: The current native install command accepts a local executable. It requires
    21: root and a running systemd system manager and does not authenticate a download
    22: or invoke `sudo` itself. Obtain and verify the candidate through a trusted
    23: channel before running it:
    24: 
    25: ```sh
    26: sudo ./wg-basic system install --candidate ./wg-basic
    27: sudo ./wg-basic system status
    28: ```
    29: 
    30: Install creates the `wg-basic` and `wg-basic-netd` service identities, installs
    31: the canonical binary and hardened service units, initializes state through the
    32: management service, then starts the services. The default management endpoint
    33: is loopback on port 8000. Set the initial administrator password from a
    34: terminal using stdin under the management UID; never place it in command-line
    35: arguments or environment variables:
    36: 
    37: ```sh
    38: printf '%s\n' 'a strong administrator password' | \
    39:   sudo -u wg-basic /usr/local/bin/wg-basic admin set-password \
    40:     --password-stdin --state [REDACTED_PATH]/wg-basic/state.db
    41: ```
    42: 
    43: Use the management UI to create the server and client, then verify client
    44: traffic before exposing the management interface through a separately
    45: configured TLS proxy.
    46: 
    47: The install receipt and service definitions are root-owned. `system status`
    48: checks their ownership and exact definitions. Install refuses foreign or
    49: modified destinations rather than replacing them.
    50: 
    51: ## Preserve state when uninstalling
    52: 
    53: Default uninstall stops the services and removes only verified wg-basic
    54: service, sysusers, receipt, and executable files:
    55: 
    56: ```sh
    57: sudo wg-basic system uninstall
    58: ```
    59: 
    60: The database at `[REDACTED_PATH]/wg-basic/state.db` and the service identities remain
    61: in place. Keeping the `wg-basic` identity preserves meaningful ownership of
    62: the secret-bearing database. Reinstall with the same command above to reuse
    63: that database and its VPN identity. Back up state before maintenance using the
    64: procedure in [State backup and restore](state-backup-restore.md).
    65: 
    66: Uninstall refuses modified or foreign files/units and does not delete the
    67: state. It is not a network teardown operation. To deliberately remove product
    68: state, first disable networking and verify convergence, then use
    69: `state purge --confirm-installation-id ...` as documented in the
    70: [operations runbook](operations-runbook.md). Once the guarded purge has
    71: removed the database, run `system uninstall` to remove the remaining system
    72: files. Keep independent backups until the appliance is no longer needed.
    73: 
    74: ## Authenticity and bootstrap trust
    75: 
    76: `release/eggpack/install.sh --version X.Y.Z` is a **lower-assurance convenience
    77: path**. It downloads and runs the exact-version installer from GitHub over
    78: HTTPS. It does not independently authenticate that bootstrap or its manifest.
    79: The wrapper prints this trust limitation before downloading. Its
    80: `--candidate --sha256 --size` mode checks file integrity against the supplied
    81: values; those values are trustworthy only after they have been compared
    82: against the release notes, and both travel over the same TLS channel, so this
    83: is integrity against corruption — not authenticity against a compromised
    84: publisher. The wrapper verifies no signatures because releases carry none.
    85: 
    86: No production key or signed release exists, by maintainer decision (see
    87: [release signing](release-signing.md)). There is therefore no
    88: independently distributed trust key and no signed high-assurance path;
    89: the strongest available procedure is the checksums-and-consistency
    90: verification below. Its anchor is the GitHub TLS delivery channel plus the
    91: published digests: it detects corruption and mix-ups, but a compromised
    92: publisher account would defeat it. Use it from a trusted Linux x86_64 or
    93: aarch64 machine:
    94: 
    95: ```sh
    96: set -eu
    97: VERSION='X.Y.Z'
    98: case "$VERSION" in ''|*[!0-9.]*|.*|*.|*..*) exit 2;; esac
    99: case "$VERSION" in *.*.*.*) exit 2;; esac
   100: VERSION_REST="${VERSION#*.}"
   101: VERSION_PATCH="${VERSION_REST#*.}"
   102: case "$VERSION" in 0[0-9]*.*|*\.0[0-9]*.*|*.*\.0[0-9]*) exit 2;; esac
   103: case "$VERSION_PATCH" in *.*) exit 2;; esac
   104: TAG="v$VERSION"
   105: BASE="https://github.com/dbowm91/wg-basic/releases/download/$TAG"
   106: WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
   107: chmod 700 "$WORK"
   108: STAGE=
   109: cleanup() { if [ -n "$STAGE" ]; then sudo rm -rf -- "$STAGE"; fi; rm -rf -- "$WORK"; }
   110: trap cleanup EXIT
   111: trap 'exit 1' HUP INT TERM
   112: curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
   113:   --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 "$BASE/release-manifest.json" \
   114:   -o "$WORK/release-manifest.json"
   115: curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
   116:   --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 "$BASE/install.sh" -o "$WORK/install.sh"
   117: # No signatures exist to check. Compare the manifest digest bindings against
   118: # the digests published in the release notes before trusting the manifest.
   119: case "$(uname -m)" in x86_64) TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu;; aarch64) TARGET=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu;; *) exit 2;; esac
   120: jq -e --arg version "$VERSION" \
   121:   '.schema_version == 1 and .product_id == "wg-basic" and .release_id == $version and (.source_revision | test("^[0-9a-f]{40}$"))' \
   122:   "$WORK/release-manifest.json" >/dev/null
   123: test "$(jq -er --arg target "$TARGET" '[.targets[] | select(.target == $target)] | length' "$WORK/release-manifest.json")" = 1
   124: SOURCE_SHA="$(jq -er '.source_revision' "$WORK/release-manifest.json")"
   125: REMOTE_TAG_REFS="$(git ls-remote "https://github.com/dbowm91/wg-basic.git" "refs/tags/$TAG" "refs/tags/$TAG^{}")"
   126: REMOTE_TAG_SHA="$(printf '%s\n' "$REMOTE_TAG_REFS" | awk -v ref="refs/tags/$TAG" '$2 == ref "^{}" {peeled=$1} $2 == ref {direct=$1} END {print peeled ? peeled : direct}')"
   127: test -n "$REMOTE_TAG_SHA" && test "$SOURCE_SHA" = "$REMOTE_TAG_SHA"
   128: git clone --quiet --depth 1 --single-branch --branch "$TAG" \
   129:   https://github.com/dbowm91/wg-basic.git "$WORK/source"
   130: test "$(git -C "$WORK/source" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$SOURCE_SHA"
   131: SOURCE_VERSION="$(git -C "$WORK/source" show HEAD:Cargo.toml | awk '
   132:   /^\[package\]$/ { in_package=1; next }
   133:   /^\[/ { in_package=0 }
   134:   in_package && /^version[[:space:]]*=/ { gsub(/"/, "", $3); print $3; exit }
   135: ')"
   136: test "$SOURCE_VERSION" = "$VERSION"
   137: ARTIFACT="$(jq -er --arg target "$TARGET" '.targets[] | select(.target == $target) | .form.artifact.name' "$WORK/release-manifest.json")"
   138: SIZE="$(jq -er --arg target "$TARGET" '.targets[] | select(.target == $target) | .form.artifact.size' "$WORK/release-manifest.json")"
   139: SHA256="$(jq -er --arg target "$TARGET" '.targets[] | select(.target == $target) | .form.artifact.sha256' "$WORK/release-manifest.json")"
   140: test "$ARTIFACT" = "wg-basic-$TARGET"
   141: case "$SIZE" in ''|*[!0-9]*) exit 2;; esac
   142: test "$SIZE" -gt 0 && test "$SIZE" -le 104857600
   143: printf '%s' "$SHA256" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'
   144: curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
   145:   --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 600 "$BASE/$ARTIFACT" -o "$WORK/wg-basic"
   146: test "$(wc -c < "$WORK/wg-basic" | tr -d '[:space:]')" = "$SIZE"
   147: printf '%s  %s\n' "$SHA256" "$WORK/wg-basic" | sha256sum --check --status
   148: case "$TARGET" in
   149:   x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) readelf -h "$WORK/wg-basic" | grep -Fq 'Advanced Micro Devices X86-64';;
   150:   aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu) readelf -h "$WORK/wg-basic" | grep -Fq 'AArch64';;
   151: esac
   152: test "$("$WORK/wg-basic" --version)" = "wg-basic $VERSION"
   153: # Stage root-owned copies and verify those exact bytes before root execution.
   154: STAGE="$(sudo mktemp -d /root/wg-basic-verified.XXXXXX)"
   155: sudo install -o root -g root -m 500 "$WORK/install.sh" "$STAGE/install.sh"
   156: sudo install -o root -g root -m 500 "$WORK/wg-basic" "$STAGE/wg-basic"
   157: sudo sh -c 'test "$(wc -c < "$1" | tr -d "[:space:]")" = "$2"' sh "$STAGE/wg-basic" "$SIZE"
   158: printf '%s  %s\n' "$SHA256" "$STAGE/wg-basic" | sudo sha256sum --check --status
   159: sudo sh "$STAGE/install.sh" --version "$VERSION" --candidate "$STAGE/wg-basic" \
   160:   --sha256 "$SHA256" --size "$SIZE"
   161: ```
   162: 
   163: The installer runs only after the manifest consistency checks and the
   164: root-owned digest rechecks above have passed. The candidate is verified
   165: against the manifest and is rechecked by the installer before
   166: `system install`. There is no publisher authentication in this path by
   167: design; fixture signatures do not qualify it further.
   168: 
   169: For current project status, see the [planning registry](../plans/registry.md).
